commentary_segments.text: For larger loop gain in the feedback loop, the distortion is lower and the input range larger. Local feedback is possible by addition of only a few transistors as shown on the left. The input transistors cannot have any AC current as they have DC current sources in both Drain and Source. Only the pMOST devices thus carry AC current. This current is determined by the differential input voltage which appears nearly unattenuated across transistor 2R. The output currents are then mirrored out. This voltage-to-current conversion is even more accurate if a full operational amplifier is inserted in the feedback loop, instead of just one single transistor. The loop gain now includes the open-loop gain of the operational amplifier. The distortion will now be very small. This is only true at low frequencies, however, as the open-loop gain of an opamp drops quite rapidly versus frequency. For high frequencies the circuit on the left may be preferable.
